clue.text: Musician's accessories lacking colour, getting the bird

parts.note: mutes are devices fitted to instruments to soften their tone
wan means pale, drained of colour

explanation.surface: A colourless musician is jeered at, or 'given the bird', along with their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' is an idiom for being booed, but here the bird is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is a common European swan species, named for being quieter than other swans.

clue.text: Visual adjustment subject to forcible separation

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges something, so the letters of the clue word are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
on can mean depending on, or subject to

explanation.surface: A tweak to an image is subject to being forcibly pulled apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Avulsion is the medical and legal term for tearing away or forcible detachment of a part.

clue.text: Ill-mannered clamour about pop group curtailed

indicators.note: the cry goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to cry is to call out loudly

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: ABBA is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: Someone rude makes a noise about a pop band being cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable and bad-tempered, much like being rude or grumpy.

clue.text: Right about blocking call for a quicker approach

indicators.note: the two short pieces sit within the call, blocking its middle

parts.note: to shout is to call out
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A correction about obstructing a phone call to speed things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cut is a faster route or method than the usual one.

clue.text: Accessory, Louis Vuitton article, containing new item of jewellery

indicators.note: the bag holds the letter for new within it

parts.note: a bag is a fashion accessory, as Louis Vuitton makes
le is the French definite article, and Louis Vuitton is a French name

explanation.surface: A designer handbag holds a new piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Louis Vuitton signals French, so the article is the French 'le'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bangle is a rigid bracelet worn on the wrist or arm.

clue.text: See 17 across
Minister backed intervening in harbour subject to tremors

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes between the letters of the harbour word

parts.note: a quay is a landing place in a harbour

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the minister abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a church minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman steps into a harbour that is shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Quavery describes something trembling or wavering, like a shaky voice.

clue.text: Leading measure when considering steam?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in front of, ahead in position
second meaning: read as '...', the quantity in the phrase '... steam'

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the phrase into A HEAD OF, as in building up a head of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of someone in a race or queue means leading them.

clue.text: Nut, losing head, with shift of active enthusiasm

indicators.note: the letter for active is moved to a new position in what remains
the first letter of the nut is dropped

parts.note: the hazel nut, or hazelnut

explanation.surface: A crazy person loses their head and has a burst of energetic keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' suggests a madman, but it is the hazel. A is the abbreviation for active (as in grammar).
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal is eager devotion or fervour for a cause.

clue.text: Take a long time consuming a lot of pretty drinks

indicators.note: the outer phrase swallows the other piece

parts.note: to be ages is to take a long time

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: pretty as in pretty good, meaning very

explanation.surface: Slowly sipping a lot of attractive drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like 'attractive' but is the adverb meaning very.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages are any drinks other than water, a formal word for things to drink.

clue.text: One in leading group savage about Liberal boasting

indicators.note: the numeral one sits inside the leading group

parts.note: the van, or vanguard, is the group at the front

indicators.note: the savage word goes around the Liberal abbreviation

parts.note: gory means bloody and brutal

explanation.surface: A person at the front rails viciously against a Liberal braggart.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglory is excessive pride and boastfulness about one's own achievements.

clue.text: Limitations on soup — cold or hot?

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

parts.note: taken as written
icy means very cold

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the soup should be served cold or hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' here means highly seasoned, not high in temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy food is hot in the sense of peppery or strongly seasoned.

clue.text: Mammal calculating tail not needed

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is not wanted

parts.note: shrewd means sharp and calculating

explanation.surface: A cunning animal can do without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrew is a small insect-eating mammal with a long pointed snout.

clue.text: On the off chance, accepting second note in additional amount

indicators.note: the phrase takes in the note, holding it within

parts.note: in case means as a precaution, on the off chance
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Speculatively taking on a second banknote to get a bit more money.
explanation.walkthrough: Note is a musical note, and do-re-mi puts re second.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise or extra amount added to something.

clue.text: Argument about recipe: he and his wife had very varying dietary tastes

definitions.text: he and his wife had very varying dietary tastes

indicators.note: the argument wraps around the recipe abbreviation

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A couple squabble over a recipe because their food preferences differ wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme: Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme ate only lean meat while his wife ate only fat.

clue.text: Beam and grate left unfinished

indicators.note: the last letter is left off

parts.note: to grate is to grind, as with cheese or teeth

explanation.surface: A wooden beam and a fireplace grate left half built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' and 'grate' look like building nouns; beam is the verb, to smile broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile widely, the same as to grin.

clue.text: A new outburst dismissing universal apprehension

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the universal abbreviation is sent away from the outburst

parts.note: a gust is a sudden burst, of wind or feeling

explanation.surface: A fresh outburst that rejects universal worry.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep anxiety or dread, a form of apprehension.

clue.text: Former area far from the coast, not island

indicators.note: not means without, so the island letter is removed

parts.note: the interior of a country is the part away from the coast

explanation.surface: An old region lies inland and not on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' looks like 'previous' in time; anterior serves for both earlier in time and further forward in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior means earlier or prior, in time as well as in position.

clue.text: It's coming now — a lot of odd ideas about oneself

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the self piece
most of the word is kept, dropping its end

parts.note: heresy is a belief against accepted doctrine
the ego is one's sense of self

explanation.surface: A rant about strange beliefs centred on oneself is about to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said just before attempting something daring, announcing it is about to start.

clue.text: Jilted bride experiencing losing no-good fraud

indicators.note: the no-good letters are taken out

parts.note: having, as in having a good time, means experiencing
NG is a common abbreviation for no good
a sham is a fake or fraud

explanation.surface: A deserted bride, losing out, was being cheated by a con.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Havisham, in Dickens's Great Expectations, was abandoned on her wedding day.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Havisham is the Dickens character who stopped all her clocks when her groom left her at the altar.

clue.text: Also (according to report) Times not open about women in couples

indicators.note: the word as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: too means also
by is the multiplication sign read aloud, as in two by three

indicators.note: the closed word goes around the women abbreviation

parts.note: a door left to is shut

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporting on closed premises and women who arrive as couples.
explanation.walkthrough: To, as in 'pull the door to', means closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two by two describes things going in pairs, as the animals entered the ark.

clue.text: Soup book is rather lacking in sex appeal

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the sex-appeal word is missing from the rather word

parts.note: quite means rather, fairly
it, as in the It girl, means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A cookbook says a soup is a bit unsexy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bisque is a rich, creamy soup, typically of shellfish.

clue.text: Key point rejected, as far as celebrity is concerned

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: to means as far as, up to
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A crucial matter is rejected where a famous person is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point on which something turns or depends.

clue.text: Turned up literary detective (not the old woman) — such writing is over the top

definitions.text: such writing is over the top

indicators.note: turned means flipped around, so the word up is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means without, so the mother letters are dropped

parts.note: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's sleuth
ma is mother, the old woman in slang

explanation.surface: Miss Marple turns up, minus her mother, in overblown prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old woman' could seem to be Miss Marple herself, but it means a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple prose is florid, ornate writing that is excessively elaborate.

clue.text: One eliminating small old city in type of game

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the game

parts.note: deer are game animals, hunted for sport
Troy was the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A wrecker drawing small ancient cities into a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is the hunted animal, not a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is someone or something that wipes out or ruins things.

clue.text: Knight getting silver, engaged in challenges in times long ago

indicators.note: the two pieces are held within the challenges

parts.note: dares are challenges to do something
K is the chess notation for king; here the knight abbreviation K

explanation.surface: A knight wins silver taking part in jousting challenges in medieval times.
explanation.walkthrough: AG is silver's chemical symbol, from Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dark Ages is the name for the early medieval period, long ago.

clue.text: See 1
See 21
Against accepting defeat? One's in the soup

indicators.note: the against word takes in the defeat word

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to admitting a loss finds themselves in trouble, or in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread floated in soup.

clue.text: Quick to carry a blade

indicators.note: the clever word carries the letter inside it

parts.note: quick-witted means clever
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quick to pick up a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed knife used by butchers.
